name: Champion
summary: A relentless warrior who pursues physical excellence in combat.
description: Champions focus on the development of martial prowess in a straightforward, rigorous style. They combine rigorous training with physical excellence to deal devastating blows.

features.name: Improved Critical
features.description: Your attack rolls with weapons and Unarmed Strikes can score a Critical Hit on a roll of 19 or 20 on the d20.

features.name: Remarkable Athlete
features.description: You have Advantage on Initiative rolls and Strength (Athletics) checks. In addition, immediately after you score a Critical Hit, you can move up to half your Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

features.name: Additional Fighting Style
features.description: You gain another Fighting Style feat of your choice.

features.name: Superior Critical
features.description: Your attack rolls with weapons and Unarmed Strikes can now score a Critical Hit on a roll of 18-20 on the d20.

features.name: Survivor
features.description: You attain the pinnacle of resilience in battle. You have Advantage on Death Saving Throws, and at the start of each of your turns you regain Hit Points equal to 5 plus your Constitution modifier if you are Bloodied and have at least 1 Hit Point.

name: Evoker
summary: A wizard who sculpts explosive elemental magic.
description: You focus your study on magic that creates powerful elemental effects such as bitter cold, searing flame, rolling thunder, crackling lightning, and burning acid.

features.name: Evocation Savant
features.description: Choose two Wizard spells from the Evocation school, each of which must be level 1 or 2, and add them to your spellbook for free.

features.name: Potent Cantrip
features.description: Your damaging cantrips affect even creatures that avoid the brunt of the effect. When a creature succeeds on a saving throw against your cantrip, the creature takes half the damage (if any) but suffers no additional effect from the cantrip.

features.name: Sculpt Spells
features.description: You can create pockets of relative safety within the effects of your evocations. When you cast an Evocation spell that affects other creatures you can see, you can choose a number of them equal to 1 plus the spell's level; the chosen creatures automatically succeed on their saving throws against the spell and take no damage if they would normally take half damage on a successful save.

features.name: Empowered Evocation
features.description: You can add your Intelligence modifier to one damage roll of any Wizard Evocation spell you cast.

features.name: Overchannel
features.description: You can increase the power of your spells. When you cast a Wizard spell of levels 1-5 that deals damage, you can deal maximum damage with it. The first time you do so, you suffer no adverse effect; using it again before you finish a Long Rest deals necrotic damage to you.

name: Life Domain
summary: Soothe the hurts of the world with the positive energy that sustains all life.
description: The Life Domain focuses on the positive energy that helps sustain all life in the multiverse. Clerics who tap into this domain are masters of healing, using that life force to cure many hurts. Existence itself relies on the positive energy associated with this domain, so a Cleric of almost any religious tradition might choose it. This domain is particularly associated with agricultural deities, gods of healing or endurance, and gods of home and community. Religious orders of healing also seek the magic of this domain.

features.name: Life Domain Spells
features.description: Your connection to this divine domain ensures you always have certain spells ready. When you reach a Cleric level specified in the Life Domain Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared. Cleric level 3: Aid, Bless, Cure Wounds, Lesser Restoration. Level 5: Mass Healing Word, Revivify. Level 7: Aura of Life, Death Ward. Level 9: Greater Restoration, Mass Cure Wounds.

features.name: Life Domain Spells (Level 5)
features.description: You always have the Mass Healing Word and Revivify spells prepared.

features.name: Life Domain Spells (Level 7)
features.description: You always have the Aura of Life and Death Ward spells prepared.

features.name: Life Domain Spells (Level 9)
features.description: You always have the Greater Restoration and Mass Cure Wounds spells prepared.

features.name: Disciple of Life
features.description: When a spell you cast with a spell slot restores Hit Points to a creature, that creature regains additional Hit Points on the turn you cast the spell. The additional Hit Points equal 2 plus the spell slot's level.

features.name: Preserve Life
features.description: As a Magic action, you present your Holy Symbol and expend a use of your Channel Divinity to evoke healing energy that can restore a number of Hit Points equal to five times your Cleric level. Choose Bloodied creatures within 30 feet of yourself (which can include you), and divide those Hit Points among them. This feature can restore a creature to no more than half its Hit Point maximum.

actions.name: Channel Divinity: Preserve Life
actions.description: Expend a use of Channel Divinity to divide up to five times your Cleric level in Hit Points among Bloodied creatures within 30 feet (up to half each target's Hit Point maximum).

features.name: Blessed Healer
features.description: The healing spells you cast on others heal you as well. Immediately after you cast a spell with a spell slot that restores Hit Points to one or more creatures other than yourself, you regain Hit Points equal to 2 plus the spell slot's level.

features.name: Supreme Healing
features.description: When you would normally roll one or more dice to restore Hit Points to a creature with a spell or Channel Divinity, don't roll those dice for the healing; instead use the highest number possible for each die. For example, instead of restoring 2d6 Hit Points to a creature with a spell, you restore 12.
